den1.motion: The camera stays locked at the drummer's shoulder. She sweeps her wire brush in small, slow circles on the snare, moving only her wrist. The singer stands still with his mouth closed. The other players and the crowd hold their places. Smoke drifts slowly above the tables. One continuous shot, no cuts.
den1.ends_on: The same framing, the brush still circling; it simply ends.
den1.why: The only motion is the small one nearest the lens, so the busy room has nothing to morph.

Thanks.

den4.motion: A locked shot. The furnace fire on the left flickers and its orange light moves softly over the bricks. A thin line of smoke rises from the cigarette in the seated man's still hand. He and the seated musicians stay motionless, mouths closed. In the final second, the camera whips left to the furnace, blurring at the peak. One continuous shot.
den4.ends_on: A fast leftward whip pan, at peak blur on the orange furnace light.
den4.why: The stillness makes this read as a band waiting, and the fire gives the whip pan a physical place to go.
den4.run:

bridge1.motion: The camera slides slowly and steadily to the left across the boat deck, at an even speed. The near black funnel passes across the frame from left to right, becoming larger, until it covers the whole lens. The band, parked cars, bridge and river keep their exact shape and stay where they are, and the cars do not move. One continuous shot, no cuts.
bridge1.ends_on: The black funnel fully covering the lens.
bridge1.why: A dark object already in the frame makes a realistic wipe, and the sideways parallax gives the wide view its life without asking anything of the small figures.
bridge1.run:

bridge2.motion: From a low position just above the water, the camera pushes forward very slowly toward the singer in the plum suit, arriving late. He stands still at the microphone, mouth closed, breathing gently. Behind him the two cars stay parked with steady headlamps and the band holds still. Dark water laps at the bottom step. In the final two seconds his jacket fills the frame. One continuous shot, no cuts.
bridge2.ends_on: The dark plum wool of his jacket filling the frame.
bridge2.why: A slow push into dark cloth gives the editor a clean exit and keeps the cars and players out of the action.
bridge2.run:

bridge3.motion: Fixed camera, symmetrical frame unchanged. The bass player and drummer play with small natural movements, and their huge shadows on the brick vault sway slightly in time with them. Nobody sings; the singer stands still with his mouth closed. Both black cars stay parked. The man in the hat stays still, a thread of smoke rising from his cigarette. Single continuous shot.
bridge3.ends_on: The same symmetrical frame with the shadows still swaying; it simply ends.
bridge3.why: The shadows carry the movement at wall scale, so the picture feels alive while the figures barely have to move.
bridge3.run:

Thanks.

bridge4.motion: The large car headlamp on the left slowly grows brighter as its filament warms, over the full eight seconds. Its glow spreads across the singer's suit and, by the end, blooms across the whole frame. The singer stays still, eyes closed, lips unmoving, not singing, his hand steady on the microphone. The players behind him and the city lights hold. One continuous shot, no cuts.
bridge4.ends_on: The headlamp's warm glare washing over the frame to near white.
bridge4.why: A single change of light avoids any risk to the close-up face and ends on a physically motivated flare.

Thanks.

mask1.motion: One continuous shot, camera locked. The man in the mustard suit slowly tilts his head to the left, pauses, then slowly tilts it to the right, admiring himself in the hand mirror, like someone trying on a hat. The tiara stays in place and the mask keeps its shape. The jeweller holds the mirror steady, mouth closed. Everyone else stays still.
mask1.ends_on: The man holding his final tilt, no camera move, a clean cut point.
mask1.why: A vain little head tilt is one small action that gets the joke across without giving the pearls, the mirror or the second man a chance to morph.
mask1.run:

mask3.motion: One continuous shot, camera locked. Snow falls and the pink flare burns. At the carriage door, the sack is lowered into the waiting man's hands and he takes its weight. Everyone else holds still, masks unchanged. Near the end, steam from under the locomotive rolls left across the frame until it fills the lens with white.
mask3.ends_on: Locomotive steam covering the whole frame, cut at full coverage.
mask3.why: The steam is already in the picture, so it gives the editor a physically motivated wipe that needs no new object.

mask4.motion: One continuous shot from the moving boat, which rides gently up and down on the water while its wake churns alongside. A thin trickle of small chips keeps falling from the tilted table into the river, and the chips keep their shape. The man with the cigar and the crowd at the rail hold still. In the last second, whip pan right along the steamer's dark hull, blurring at the peak.
mask4.ends_on: A short rightward whip pan, cut at peak blur.
mask4.why: Earlier falling objects morphed, so the fall is reduced to a thin trickle and the boat's gentle motion carries the life of the shot.
mask4.run:

safe4.motion: Inside the rocking car, the only thing that changes is the light. Through the cracked oval rear window, the two headlamps slowly grow brighter and nearer, drifting a little from side to side. The blind's tassel sways with the road. The man stays frozen, his head and gloved hands unmoving, his mask unchanged. One continuous shot. Finally the window burns white and flares across the lens.
safe4.ends_on: Headlamp glare blooming from the rear window until the lens flares out.
safe4.why: Telling the chase entirely through light keeps the masked figure and his hands still, and the flare hands the editor a bright exit.

chase2.motion: Locked off on the rooftop, one continuous shot. Far below, the tiny yellow 1920s roadster, with its separate mudguards, running boards and spoked wheels, drives steadily left along the road and out across the junction, a little dust trailing behind it. It stays the same car. The tram, other cars and pedestrians wait where they are. In the last second, the camera pans quickly left until the dark iron leg of the water tank fills the lens.
chase2.ends_on: The tank's dark iron leg covering the frame, cut at full coverage.
chase2.why: Last time's slide, pursuit and hurrying crowd are removed so a single tiny car can stay period-correct and hold its shape, with a dark object already in the frame as the way out.
